newsitem.title: DUBAI: ADNOC delays portion of Ruwais expansion - MEES.
newsitem.headline: ADNOC delays portion of Ruwais expansion - MEES.

text.p: Abu Dhabi National Oil Company (ADNOC) has delayed for three to five years a major portion of a planned second phase expansion of its Ruwais refinery, the Middle East Economic Survey (MEES) reported on Monday.
"The delay affects most, although not all, of the units contemplated under the ambitious $1.2 billion upgrading program," the Cyprus-based weekly said.
The second phase expansion was envisaged to promote Abu Dhabi's exports of refined products, particularly middle distillates, by doubling plant capacity.
Facilities delayed at the 135,000 barrels per day (bpd) Ruwais plant will be a planned new crude unit, a vacuum distillation unit, a hydrocracker and a coker, MEES said.
Plans to bring on units that would improve gasoline and naphtha yields are unaffected.

Phase one expansion plans -- involving the construction of two condenate distillation trains at a cost of some $200 million at Ruwais-- are also facing a delay of six months from their original 1998 start up, MEES reported.
Companies submitted their initial proposals for phase one expansion in July.

Industry sources in the UAE told Reuters this month that the project delays were tied to an overall rethink by ADNOC of its oil and petrochemical downstream policy which coincided with the appointment of a new acting project director at ADNOC.
A source at Ruwais said no final decision had yet been made on how to proceed with the first phase expansion of the plant involving the new condensate trains.
